convention.frame: x forward, y left, z up, metres; the hull box is centred on x = 0, y = 0 and stands on z = 0
convention.hull_box: the top is max(the real hull or turret roof, the top of the tallest bulky dressing - 0.3 m) (decisions.md C4, after F-B1). Sights, sensors, radars and roof guns that are not a roster mount are dressing, held to unitArt.ts's 0.3 m bulky / 0.15 m thin allowance. The box covers the body, including an armoured turret overhang (FC8)
convention.pivot: the centre of the turret ring; for a fixed mount, the trunnion or hinge it is drawn on (only pivot + muzzle reaches the simulation)
convention.muzzle: muzzle_m is measured from the mount's pivot: the simulation fires from pivot + muzzle (crates/sim/src/weapons/muzzle.rs:12-22; decisions.md C5)
convention.eye: the sight's height over the ground (catalog.rs:181); kept unless a source contradicts it (FA-6)

thresholds.hull_dimension: fix when off by more than max(0.10 m, 3 %)
thresholds.pivot: fix when off by more than 0.15 m on any axis
thresholds.muzzle_point: fix when the world muzzle point (pivot + muzzle) is off by more than 0.15 m on any axis; a value written in another convention is fixed whatever its size (C5)
thresholds.eye_m: kept unless a source contradicts it
thresholds.note: One set for every lane (decisions.md C10). The lanes' own variants (F-A's max(0.10 m, 3 %) for muzzles, F-C's 0.30 m muzzle reach) are retired.

verdicts.keep: the frame number agrees with the references within the thresholds
verdicts.fix: slice 15 changes it to `new`: a row in fix-rows.json, or the parent's row where the fixture takes the field through extends
verdicts.unresolved: kept at today's value: nothing measures it well enough to move it; named
verdicts.art-only: not a frame number: the family slice fixes the art
verdicts.inherits: the fixture extends another unit and this appearance takes its rows

sources.note: nose right, launcher and radar raised. Hull 1391 px. The turret (radar at the front, launcher behind it) spans 0.43 to 1.03 of the hull length from the tail; its base box centres at 0.73. Rear drive sprocket, engine deck behind the turret
confirms the layout: a low engine deck at the rear, the turret forward with the radar facing forward, the launcher hinged at the turret's rear

9A317 TELAR 8.0 x 3.3 x 3.8 m; the same figure is repeated for most vehicles of the system, so it is weak. Other sources give 9.3 x 3.25 x 3.8 m for the M1/M2 TELAR; none was found for the M3's 9A317M

art.note: tier 0 of the committed GLB: hull is what fit.hull_extents measures (no gun, hmg or dressing_* subtree); crew and antennas are left out of the dressing column

rows.source: militarytoday Buk-M3 (about 65 km/h on roads); the Gepard's tracked block
rows.note: C6: the simulation drives it on tracks, not wheels: the Gepard's tracked block (65 km/h on roads, which the Buk-M3 shares), and no turning radius.

C6: the Buk-M3 rides the tracked GM-569; it takes the profile the other tracked air defence and IFV units extend (the Gepard, the M2A4, the CV9040C, the BMP-3). The two profiles hold the same sensors and sound, so the profile name alone changes nothing; the mobility row below is what moves.

rows.source: armyrecognition Buk-M3 9K317M data sheet: 9.3 x 3.25 x 3.8 m (also the M1/M2 TELAR's)
rows.note: C6: 9.3 m, the best-sourced published length (the M3's own data sheet; 8.0 m is a figure the same site repeats for most of the system's vehicles). Inside the tracked cap (half-length 4.8 m). Lane: No trustworthy published dimension; the photos have no scale. But 9.75 m is past the tracked cap (4.8 m half-length), which matters once the mobility is fixed (see findings); 9.3 m is the best-supported figure then

3.25 m against 3.2 m: inside 0.10 m. Lane: No trustworthy published dimension; the photos have no scale. But 9.75 m is past the tracked cap (4.8 m half-length), which matters once the mobility is fixed (see findings); 9.3 m is the best-supported figure then

C4: box top = max(roof, tallest bulky dressing - 0.3 m). The folded radar is a sensor, so dressing (F-B6): 3.8 - 0.3 = 3.5 m, inside 0.10 m of today's 3.56 m. The turret roof is unmeasured. Lane: No trustworthy published dimension; the photos have no scale. But 9.75 m is past the tracked cap (4.8 m half-length), which matters once the mobility is fixed (see findings); 9.3 m is the best-supported figure then

The frame and the art put the turret at the rear behind a cab; the real TELAR's turret stands forward of mid-hull over a rear engine deck, its base centred about 0.23 of the hull length ahead of the middle
In travel the six containers lie on the turret with their noses forward against the radar's back face, about x 2.3 m and z 3.3 m (old world point [0.05, 0, 2.96] m)

overlays.note: No drawing of the Buk-M3 exists free; the-blueprints.com sells vectors only. No generated view was made: the open questions are the layout and the length, and a generated view would guess both.

notes.why: Beyond detail, the layout is wrong: the model draws a crew cab at the front and the launcher on a turret at the rear; the real 9A317M has no cab, a large forward turret carrying the radar in front and the six-container launcher behind it, and a low engine deck at the rear. Slice 24's buk.py rebuilds the layout first, then adds the radar, rails and fittings.; frame part: the launcher pivot and muzzle (fix), and the mobility and length (unresolved)
